Fresh mulch is one of the fastest ways to make your entire property look sharper and more put-together. It’s like a fresh haircut for your landscape beds. But beyond just looking good, a proper layer of mulch is one of the best things you can do for your plants, your soil, and even your water bill. Here in Omaha, where our weather can swing from one extreme to another, mulch provides a much-needed buffer, protecting your plants from the scorching Nebraska sun and helping the soil hold onto moisture during those dry spells. My name is Bryan, and at A1 Junk Removal and Tree Service, we’ve been helping homeowners all over the Omaha area—from Benson to Bellevue—keep their properties looking great with our straightforward, no-nonsense mulching services.

More Than Just a Pretty Face: What Mulch Really Does for Your Yard

It’s easy to think of mulch as just decorative ground cover, but it’s a real workhorse for your garden beds. A good 2-3 inch layer of quality mulch does a whole lot more than just look nice. It’s a critical part of maintaining healthy soil and happy plants, especially with our unpredictable Nebraska weather patterns. It acts like a shield, keeping the soil cooler in the summer and warmer in the winter, which means less stress on your plant roots. Plus, it’s one of the best ways to keep weeds from taking over your beautiful flower beds. If you're tired of constantly pulling weeds, our weed control services combined with fresh mulch can make a world of difference.

Photo coming soon

Choosing the Right Mulch for Your Omaha Property

Walk into any garden center and the choices can be overwhelming. Cedar, cypress, hardwood, dyed black, red, brown... what's the difference? The truth is, the type of mulch you choose does matter. For most residential beds in the Omaha area, we find that a good quality, double-shredded hardwood or cedar mulch is the best all-around choice. It mats together nicely to stay in place, does a great job of suppressing weeds, and breaks down over time to add valuable organic matter to our heavy clay soil. We can help you decide what’s best for your specific plants and the look you’re going for. We source our mulch locally, so you're getting a product that's meant to perform well right here in our climate.

Our Mulch Installation Process: Clean, Crisp, and Done Right

There’s a right way and a wrong way to lay down mulch. Just dumping it in a pile and spreading it around can lead to problems like suffocated plants or rot against your foundation. We take the time to do it right. Our process is clean and efficient, leaving you with sharp, professional-looking landscape beds without any of the hassle. We make sure the job is done right from start to finish, so you can just enjoy the results.

Bed Preparation: We'll start by cleaning out any weeds, leaves, and old, decomposed mulch to create a clean slate for the new layer.

Crisp Edging: We redefine the edges of your flower beds for a sharp, clean line between your lawn and your landscape areas.

Quality Mulch Delivery: We deliver your choice of high-quality mulch directly to your property.

Professional Installation: We carefully apply a consistent 2-3 inch layer of mulch, ensuring it's not piled up against plant stems or your home's foundation.

Thorough Cleanup: Once the mulch is down, we blow off all patios, walkways, and driveways to leave your property looking immaculate.

Frequently Asked Questions

How often should I have new mulch put down?

For most properties in the Omaha area, we recommend a fresh layer of mulch once a year, usually in the spring. This ensures your beds look great and the mulch is deep enough to continue providing benefits like weed suppression and moisture retention.

What's the difference between all the types of mulch?

The main differences are aesthetics and longevity. Hardwood mulches are a great all-around choice, while cedar has the added benefit of repelling some insects. We can discuss the pros and cons of each and help you pick the best one for your yard and budget.

Can you just deliver mulch for me to spread myself?

While our main service is full installation, we can sometimes arrange for mulch-only delivery depending on our schedule. However, most homeowners find that having our crew handle the spreading saves them a ton of time and back-breaking work.

Is it okay to put new mulch on top of old mulch?

Yes, as long as the old layer isn't too thick. We typically remove any excess, matted-down old mulch to ensure the total depth doesn't exceed 3-4 inches, which can prevent water from reaching the soil.
